newsitem.title: USA: Stocks jump as interest rate pressures ease.
newsitem.headline: Stocks jump as interest rate pressures ease.

text.p: Stocks tallied solid gains Tuesday, boosted by lower long-term interest rates and optimism about the outlook for inflation and corporate earnings.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 45.41 points at 6,754.59, surpassing Monday's record close of 6,709.18.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 13.62 points at 1,344.53 while the American Stock Exchange index rose 1.22 to 587.35.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 16-7 on active volume of 294 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Stocks got their primary lift from a bond market rally that was sparked by a lower-than-expected increase in consumer prices for December.
The Labour Department reported the Consumer Price Index rose 0.3 percent in December, in line with analysts' expectations.

More important, said analysts, was a surprisingly small increase when volatile food and energy prices were excluded. The so-called "core" CPI rose only 0.1 percent, a smaller gain than economists had forecast.
"The CPI looks like a clear signal things are on the right track and appears to have relaxed interest rate concerns," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up more than three-quarters of a point, lowering its yield to 6.78 percent from Monday's 6.85 percent. The yield and the price move in opposite directions.
While the drop in bond yields clearly helped stocks, analysts said they preferred to see more progress before they called the interest rate picture a favourable one.

"I think we could see a rally past 6.75 percent and I think that's a threshold level," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital. "If we don't get through 6.75 percent, we're at extreme risk that one bad number could get us all the way to 7 percent."
Financial stocks were among the strongest performers, helped by upbeat earnings and the improved interest rate outlook. Citicorp was up 3-7/8 at 104-3/8, and J.P. Morgan gained 5/8 to 103-1/8.
Technology stocks were also solid, led by semiconductor chip giant, Intel Corp., which was due to report earnings after the close. Intel was up 2 at 148-7/8.
"Intel hasn't disappointed in a long time," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Another gainer was chip maker Advanced Micro Devices Inc., which received a vote of confidence, when SoundView Financial issued a buy rating on company's stock, which jumped 4 to 33.

The stock of health maintenance organisations or HMOs were weaker on fears the United States would move to slow premium growth rates. Oxford Health Plans Inc. fell 2-3/4 to 52-5/8 and United Healthcare Corp. lost 1 to 43-1/4.
Payless ShoeSource Inc. jumped 2-1/2 to 37-1/8 after the company announced it would acquire J. Baker Inc.'s Parade of Shoes unit for undisclosed terms.
